title: Did Urmila Sleep for 14 Years?
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1.70-76, with a whole-text search (Critical Edition)

captions.instagram:
Did Urmila really sleep for fourteen years?

Part 1 of 2. A much-loved story says Urmila slept for fourteen years so that Lakshmana could stay awake and guard his brother. In Valmiki's Ramayana (Critical Edition), Urmila is named at her wedding: Janaka gives "Sita to Rama, Urmila to Lakshmana" and tells Lakshmana, "Come, take Urmila's hand." She is named once more, when Sita tells Anasuya of her marriage. There is no Nidra Devi and no 14-year sleep anywhere in the text. The story is told with love for Urmila's sacrifice. Part 2: what Valmiki says about Lakshmana's nights.

Did you grow up hearing Urmila slept for 14 years? 👇 Part 2: Lakshmana's nights. Jai Shri Ram!

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1.70-76, with a whole-text search (Critical Edition)
Verses:
• Janaka gives Sita to Rama and Urmila to Lakshmana — 1.70.21-22; 1.72.18
• At the wedding Janaka says: Lakshmana, come, accept Urmila whom I offer; take her hand — 1.72.18
• Lakshmana's wife Urmila is named only at the wedding (Bala 70-76) and once by Sita to Anasuya (2.110.51); nowhere else in the CE — 1.70.21-22, 1.71.3, 1.72.18, 1.76.9; 2.110.51
• No Nidra Devi and no 14-year sleep of Urmila (or 14-year wakefulness of Lakshmana) in the CE — whole text searched (all 7 kandas)
• The Urmila / Nidra Devi story is a later, loving telling (no single text named or quoted) — later folk tellings

verify_note: Whole CE searched (Bala 76, Ayodhya 111, Aranya 71, Kishkindha 66, Sundara 66, Yuddha 116, Uttara 100 sargas): ऊर्मिला only at 1.70.21-22, 1.71.3, 1.72.18, 1.76.9 and 2.110.51 (1.32.12 is another Urmila, a gandharvi's mother). No Nidra Devi, no 14-year sleep. Nights: 1 Tamasa 2.41.12-14 (Lakshmana awake all night with Sumantra); 2 Shringaverapura 2.44.25-26, 2.45.2-3 (Guha offers the bed), 2.45.9 (Lakshmana's reply); 3 under a tree past the Ganga 2.47.1-3 (Rama: we two must keep awake); 4 Bharadvaja 2.48-49.1; 5 by the Yamuna 2.49.15; morning 2.50.1-3 Rama gently wakes the sleeping Lakshmana.
